correctness.rationale: Finite abelian Fourier transform is invertible because char K∤|A| and K contains all exponent(A)-roots. The convolution transform formula gives F(u*v)(χ)=F(u)(Φχ)F(v)(Ψχ). If f in a two-sided ideal has nonzero coordinate α, choose right factor δ_{ΨΦ^{-1}α} to extract f(α)δ_{Φ^{-1}α}. Multiplying coordinate vectors on right and on left yields δ_{Φ^{-1}β} and δ_{Ψ^{-1}β}; finite-order permutations propagate to the whole H orbit. Thus arbitrary ideal subspaces are coordinate-orbit sums, not assumed diagonally decomposed. Conversely H-orbit spans are two-sided ideals; distinct orbits annihilate, δ_{Φχ}*δ_{Ψχ}=δ_χ shows each block square generates itself, and any nonzero subideal contains an entire block. For Rp, dual nonzero indices are cosets of <-1,2> and zero singleton; p31 gives h=10. Independent exact prime-orbit tests p=3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23,31 confirm dimensions; general proof not inferred from examples.

originality.rationale: The Fourier multiplication identity is previously established, as are substantial one-sided module decompositions and augmentation/commutator ideal facts. The submitted new step is a complete two-sided-ideal classification: arbitrary ideal vectors are forced to contain individual Fourier coordinates, then both dual automorphisms propagate to whole orbits; these orbit blocks are simple and mutually annihilate. The argument is not a re-labeling of right-simple constituents. Full literature priority remains qualified because the newest Ta preprint was inaccessible beyond summary and institutional storage was exhausted.

value.rationale: A complete classification of all two-sided ideals and simple nonassociative blocks in a natural infinite class of finite latin Alexander quandle algebras supplies an algebraic structural theorem, a Boolean lattice formula and exact arithmetic ideal counts. Explains why right-simple representation constituents do not directly classify two-sided ideals; likely useful for future quandle-ring simplicity and augmentation studies.
